issues.failure_explanation: The proof of item (2) bounds the p-th moment of the compensated Levy stochastic integral by C times the p/2-th power of its PREDICTABLE quadratic variation, invoking the Burkholder--Davis--Gundy inequality. BDG controls moments of a martingale by its (optional) quadratic variation, which for a jump martingale contains the sum of squared jump sizes; the displayed bound holds only for continuous (Wiener) martingales. For a compensated compound-Poisson component with intensity eps and jumps of size a, E|integral|^p is of order eps*a^p/Lambda (one jump near time t), not of order (eps*a^2/Lambda)^{p/2}; hence the jump part of the second Rosenthal term, sum (1+lambda)^{rho p/2} E|I|^p, can diverge even when L in L^p(Omega,H^eta) is finite. Concrete counterexample within the stated hypotheses: eta = -1/2, p = 4, independent compensated compound-Poisson components L_{ell,m} with intensity eps_l = l^{-3/2} and jumps +/-1. Then E||L(1)||^2_{H^eta} ~ sum (2l+1) l^{-1} l^{-3/2} < inf (Assumption 2.1 holds) and E||L(1)||^4_{H^eta} < inf (independence + finite fourth moments per component), yet E||tilde L(1)||^4_{H^{0.4}} >= sum_{ell,m} (1+lambda)^{2rho} E|I_{ell,m}(1)|^4, and since E|I|^4 >= c*eps_l/lambda_l (single jump in a window of width ~1/lambda near t), the summand behaves like (2l+1)*l^{1.6-1.5-2} = l^{-0.9}, whose sum diverges. Thus ||X(1)||_{L^4(Omega,H^{0.4})} = infinity while rho - eta = 0.9 <= 1, so the stated estimate is false. (Additionally, the intermediate chain step E|L_{ell,m}(1)|^p >= E|L_{ell,m}(1)-tilde m|^p + |tilde m_{ell,m}|^p is invalid as written, though the needed lower bound follows by Jensen/Lyapunov.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must weaken item (2) to the range rho - eta < 2/p (as in item (3), provable by the same Rosenthal inequality with the jump-moment term retained), or add a hypothesis controlling the p-th jump moments (e.g. uniformly bounded jump sizes with summable intensities), and correspondingly restrict Corollary cor:added-1's first display; items (1) and (3) and all other results are unaffected.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition prop:regul's item (2) for p>2 is false: no H^rho bound with rho-eta<=1 follows from L in L^p(Omega,H^eta) plus independence of the components. The dependent Corollary cor:added-1 (first display: weak convergence with rate kappa^{-2(eta+1)} for Levy noise with independent components) loses its supporting regularity input and is unsupported; likewise the surrounding prose claims that the Assumption-ass:TestFunc class is nontrivial for this setting and that Poisson weak rates are p-independent become unreliable.
issues.title: L2-regularity estimate for jump Levy noise with independent components is false (BDG misapplied to discontinuous martingales)
issues.why_classification: The stated regularity result is false for p>2 (counterexample above), so item (2) must be abandoned or its regime restricted to rho-eta <= 2/p or to p=2; the dependent weak-rate guarantee of Corollary cor:added-1 (rate 2(eta+1) for Levy noise) is lost, since the surviving range only gives eta+1+rho with rho < eta+1/m. This excludes an advertised regime and materially worsens the weak-rate guarantee; no source-supported repair preserves it.

issues.failure_explanation: The numerics describe the simulated field by L_{ell,m} ~ l^{-alpha} Lhat_{l,m}, i.e. amplitude decay l^{-alpha}, which instantiates Assumption ass:SpecialLevyProcess with parameter 2alpha (there a_ell <= C l^{-alpha/2}, variance decay l^{-2alpha}). Under this literal reading, Theorem Thm:ConvEM predicts a strong Euler–Maruyama rate h^{min{alpha/2,1}} and Theorem Thm:ConvEM2 a second-moment rate h^{min{alpha,1}}, so the quoted expected rates h^{min{alpha/4,1/2}} and h^{min{alpha/2,1}} are smaller by a factor 2 than what the cited theorems give for the described processes. Conversely, if alpha is meant to be the Assumption-ass:SpecialLevyProcess parameter (variance decay l^{-alpha}), then the described scaling l^{-alpha} is wrong, and the quoted strong-error cap 1/2 still contradicts Theorem Thm:ConvEM, whose bound is h^{min{beta/2,1}} with cap 1. The same symbol alpha is used with two incompatible meanings (the covariance-decay reading appears in the discussion of Figure wr figures), so the numerical confirmation claims are not supported by the theorems as stated.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the simulation scaling in the convention of Assumption ass:SpecialLevyProcess (amplitude l^{-alpha/2} for parameter alpha) and correct the quoted expected Euler–Maruyama strong rate to h^{min{alpha/4,1}} (equivalently, keep the quoted rates and correct the description of L_{ell,m} and re-derive the rates under the amplitude convention); no theoretical result is affected.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed numerical validation of Theorem L:SA1, Thm:ConvEM and Thm:ConvEM2 (Figures fig:SEem, fig:MEem, fig:SmEem and the spectral/weak-rate figures) is not verifiable against the theorems: the simulated processes, as described, obey different theoretical rates (by a factor 2, or a different cap) than those quoted, so the experimental 'confirmation' claims are unreliable as stated.
issues.title: Numerical section's noise scaling and quoted expected rates are inconsistent with the cited theorems
issues.why_classification: A short, local correction of the parameter convention in Section sec:Num (and of the misquoted cap 1/2 to 1) restores full consistency; all theorems, rates, and guarantees of the paper remain valid, so the repair is local and routine with no mathematical loss.
